earlier_failures.reason: Compositor-selected window produced an address-bar mask wider than the 1024-pixel axis cap. No native frame verified. Original binary and original frozen fixtures retained by hash; fixture bytes preserved.

At controlled 1180x880 the original two-background fixture exceeded the unchanged four-million work cap. That exact HTML is now the explicit overdraw-fallback fixture. Original host source and fixture bytes retained.

validation.cpu_reference: Complete original Canvas painter; differential reference, not an independent raster oracle
validation.current_ci: Pending publication; local results are not represented as CI results.

limits.accounting_scope: Explicit resources and vector capacities; not process RSS. Excludes driver/allocator/surface storage, borrowed page/image assets, font caches, trusted font-outline allocations and CPU-fallback temporaries.

claim_boundaries: The browser uses the custom GPU kernels for admitted scenes; rounded geometry and glyph coverage remain CPU-prepared.
Normal native packets have no CPU framebuffer/reference/readback; explicit verification carries one complete Canvas reference.
Unsupported scenes use the complete original CPU painter and upload route. Fallback runs establish route/admission, not acquired fallback pixel equality.
Only 4,153,600 active acquired-texture bytes are counted in this checkpoint. Padding, normal runs, fallback and reload contribute no comparison bytes.
Reload evidence establishes a new confined worker after actual GPU presentation and generation-two scene preparation; no second-presentation claim.
Opacity verification deliberately exits 1 with 0/1 quota and is a successful refusal check, not a successful native frame.
Native-window checks cover one selected NVIDIA adapter and BGRA8 surface before the compositor; older multi-adapter offscreen evidence is separate.
No Chromium performance comparison, complete web compatibility or independent production security assurance is established.
